module_title: Himalayan Rivers - Tributaries and Major Treaties
introduction: At this level, we focus on the major right-bank and left-bank tributaries of these massive river systems and the historical water-sharing agreements that govern them.

core_concepts.title: Tributaries of Ganga
core_concepts.description: Right Bank: Yamuna (longest tributary, originates from Yamunotri), Son, and Punpun. Left Bank: Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi, and Mahananda.

core_concepts.title: Tributaries of Indus
core_concepts.description: It has five major tributaries known as the 'Panjnad': Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej. (Chenab is the largest tributary of the Indus).

core_concepts.title: Tributaries of Brahmaputra
core_concepts.description: Right Bank: Subansiri (largest), Kameng, Manas, Sankosh, and Teesta. Left Bank: Dibang, Lohit (known as the river of blood), and Dhansiri.

core_concepts.title: Indus Water Treaty (1960)
core_concepts.description: A water-distribution treaty between India and Pakistan brokered by the World Bank. India got 100% exclusive rights over the 3 Eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej), while Pakistan got 80% of the water from the 3 Western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab), with India retaining 20% for limited use.

important_entities.name: Kosi River
important_entities.significance: The Kosi River (a left-bank tributary of the Ganga) is notorious for frequently changing its course (shifting channels) and causing devastating floods, earning it this tragic title.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Almost all Himalayan tributaries originate in the mountains. However, the 'Gomti' is a major exception; it originates in the plains from 'Fulhar Lake' in Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh.
Not all of the 'Panjnad' rivers originate in India. The 'Sutlej' originates from 'Rakas Lake' (Rakshastal) in Tibet and enters India (Himachal Pradesh) through the Shipki La pass.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej. This perfectly maps their North-to-South geographical alignment.

exam_strategy_tips: Examiners love to confuse students with Right vs. Left bank tributaries of the Ganga. Always remember Yamuna and Son are the major RIGHT bank tributaries.
A frequent treaty question: 'Which rivers are under India's control per the Indus Water Treaty?' Answer: The Eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej).
